_meta.why: Ashwin, 2026-09-10: 'why haven't we been tracking Mercosur, ECOWAS, or some of these other more subregional organizations?' The original eighteen come from the international_orgs.csv workbook; these ride in from this file via scripts/build-orgs-extra.py so the workbook is untouched. Members are named as countries.json names them and resolved to slugs at build time; a name that does not resolve fails the build rather than vanishing.
_meta.statuses: Member = full member. Partner = associate or associated state. Observer = observer. Suspended memberships are omitted.
_meta.verified: 2026-09-10: every organisation on the site (the workbook's eighteen and these) checked against its own site, Wikipedia's current membership page or recent news by three research passes; corrections applied here and, for the workbook's organisations, in `overrides` below.

orgs.label: Southern Common Market
orgs.desc: South American customs union; Bolivia became the fifth full member in 2024, Venezuela has been suspended since 2017.

orgs.label: Economic Community of West African States
orgs.desc: West African economic community; twelve members since Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger completed their withdrawal in January 2025.

orgs.label: Alliance of Sahel States
orgs.desc: Confederation of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger under the July 2024 treaty, formed on leaving ECOWAS.

orgs.label: Southern African Development Community
orgs.desc: Sixteen southern African states from Angola and DR Congo to South Africa and Madagascar.

orgs.label: East African Community
orgs.desc: Eight partner states with a customs union and common market, and a proposed political federation; Somalia joined in 2024.

orgs.label: Economic Community of Central African States
orgs.desc: Eleven central African states from Chad to Angola.

orgs.label: Intergovernmental Authority on Development
orgs.desc: Horn of Africa bloc of seven; Eritrea rejoined in 2023 and withdrew again in December 2025.

orgs.label: Arab Maghreb Union
orgs.desc: Five Maghreb states; largely dormant since the 1990s over the Western Sahara dispute.

orgs.label: Caribbean Community
orgs.desc: Fifteen Caribbean members including Guyana, Suriname and Haiti; Montserrat is a member but not a country here.

orgs.label: Central American Integration System
orgs.desc: Eight Central American and Caribbean states, the Dominican Republic included.

orgs.label: Andean Community
orgs.desc: Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru; Chile and the Mercosur states are associates.

orgs.label: Bolivarian Alliance for the Peoples of Our America
orgs.desc: Venezuela and Cuba's alliance of ten, mostly Caribbean, states; Bolivia's membership was suspended after its 2025 election.

orgs.label: Pacific Islands Forum
orgs.desc: Eighteen Pacific members from Australia and New Zealand to the atoll states; French Polynesia and New Caledonia are members but not countries here.

orgs.label: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
orgs.desc: Eight South Asian states; summits have been stalled since 2014 by the India-Pakistan dispute.

orgs.label: Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation
orgs.desc: Seven states around the Bay of Bengal, the grouping India has favoured over SAARC.

orgs.label: Eurasian Economic Union
orgs.desc: Russia-led economic union of five with a common market; observers include Uzbekistan and Cuba.

orgs.label: Commonwealth of Independent States
orgs.desc: Post-Soviet association; Ukraine and Georgia have left, Moldova gave notice in April 2026 and leaves in April 2027, Turkmenistan is an associate.

orgs.label: Organization of Turkic States
orgs.desc: Five Turkic-speaking states; Hungary and Turkmenistan observe.

orgs.label: European Free Trade Association
orgs.desc: The four European states outside the EU with single-market access: Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland.

orgs.label: Nordic Council
orgs.desc: The five Nordic states with the Faroe Islands, Greenland and Åland; a parliamentary body since 1952.

orgs.label: Benelux Union
orgs.desc: Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg; the 1944 customs union that preceded the EU.

orgs.label: Visegrád Group
orgs.desc: Czechia, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia; a political grouping since 1991.

orgs.label: United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement
orgs.desc: The 2020 successor to NAFTA.

orgs.label: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership
orgs.desc: Twelve Pacific-rim economies; the United Kingdom acceded in December 2024 and Costa Rica's accession working group concluded in May 2026.

orgs.label: Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership
orgs.desc: The ten ASEAN states with Australia, China, Japan, New Zealand and South Korea; the largest trade bloc by population.

overrides._why: Corrections to the WORKBOOK organisations (international_orgs.csv is their source and was not edited). Applied after the merge: a status string sets it, null removes the membership. Move these into the workbook when it is next edited and delete them here.
_notes: OPEC / OPEC+: the UAE withdrew effective 1 May 2026 (Enerdata, Khaleej Times).
SCO: Laos became the fifteenth dialogue partner at the 2025 Tianjin summit.
African Union: six suspensions in force (Mali 2021, Sudan 2021, Burkina Faso 2022, Niger 2023, Madagascar 2025, Guinea-Bissau 2025); Gabon (April 2025) and Guinea (January 2026) reinstated.
OAS: Nicaragua's withdrawal took effect 19 November 2023.
Commonwealth: Gabon (suspension lifted July 2025), Togo (joined 2022), St Kitts & Nevis and St Vincent were missing from the workbook.

Kept as Member with a caveat: Armenia in the CSTO (participation frozen since 2024, no formal withdrawal); Saudi Arabia in BRICS+ (invited, still 'assessing'); Moldova in the CIS (leaves April 2027); Cuba in the OAS (member, non-participating).

2026-09-10 Wikidata tripwire, first run: São Tomé and Príncipe was missing from the UN and the African Union, St Kitts & Nevis and St Vincent from the UN and the OAS (all four are members; workbook rows never filled).
